topic: Why props cavitate — and what that rumble is doing to your propeller

phrases: That rumble from your propeller? It could be water boiling. In cool sea water.
A propeller blade works like a wing. As it spins, the pressure on its back face drops.
Drop pressure low enough, and water boils, even when it's cool.
Tiny vapour bubbles form on the blade. That's cavitation.
Then the bubbles reach higher pressure and collapse, violently, right against the metal.
Millions of tiny hammer blows eat pits into the blade. Mechanics call it cavitation burn.
You feel vibration, hear a rumble, and lose top speed at the same RPM.
Common causes: nicked or bent blades, marine growth, or the wrong pitch for your boat.
So keep blades smooth and clean, and have the prop checked by a specialist.
And if a clean, undamaged prop still cavitates, a different prop design can solve it.
Ever heard your prop rumble? Tell us in the comments.

title: Why Your Propeller Rumbles: Cavitation Explained
research: https://www.westmarine.com/west-advisor/propeller-cavitation-vs-ventilation.html (cavitation = low pressure on the back of the blade forms vapour bubbles that collapse violently against the metal -> pitting/'cavitation burn'; symptoms: vibration rising with RPM, rattling/knocking, loss of top speed at full RPM; causes: nicked/bent/corroded edges, too much pitch, marine growth/fishing line, RPM beyond design; fixes: recondition/replace, correct pitch, clean, cupped/higher-load design; ventilation is surface air, a different problem)
Physics: water boils when local pressure falls to its vapour pressure, so it can boil at sea temperature (100 C only at normal atmospheric pressure).

caption_en: That rumble from your propeller could be water boiling, in cool sea water. 🌊 A prop blade works like a wing: as it spins, pressure on its back face drops. Drop pressure low enough and water boils even when it's cool, forming tiny vapour bubbles: that's cavitation. When the bubbles reach higher pressure they collapse violently against the metal, and millions of tiny hammer blows eat pits into the blade ('cavitation burn'). Signs: vibration, a rumble, and less top speed at the same RPM. Common causes: nicked or bent blades, marine growth, or the wrong pitch for your boat. Keep blades smooth and clean, have the prop checked by a specialist, and if a clean, undamaged prop still cavitates, a different prop design can solve it. Ever heard your prop rumble? caption_ar: هل تسمع هديرًا من مروحة قاربك؟ قد يكون الماء يغلي… في مياه البحر الباردة! 🌊 شفرة المروحة تعمل مثل جناح الطائرة: أثناء دورانها ينخفض الضغط على ظهرها. وعندما ينخفض الضغط بما يكفي يغلي الماء حتى وهو بارد، فتتكوّن فقاعات بخار صغيرة، وهذا ما يسمّى «التكهّف». وعندما تصل الفقاعات إلى منطقة ضغط أعلى تنفجر للداخل بعنف ملاصقةً للمعدن، وملايين الضربات الصغيرة تحفر نقرًا في الشفرة يسميها الفنيون «حرق التكهّف». العلامات: اهتزاز، وهدير، وانخفاض السرعة القصوى عند نفس عدد الدورات. أشهر الأسباب: شفرات مخدوشة أو منحنية، أو نموّ بحري، أو خطوة مروحة غير مناسبة لقاربك. حافظ على الشفرات ناعمة ونظيفة، واطلب فحص المروحة من مختص، وإذا استمر التكهّف مع مروحة نظيفة وسليمة فقد يكون الحل تصميم مروحة مختلف. هل سمعت هدير مروحتك من قبل؟ أخبرنا في التعليقات 👇 وتابع Creative Tracks Marine لشرح جديد عن القوارب كل يومين.
